summary: Iteration 49 — Phase MKT.3 (Winner Notifications + Featured Listings) tested end-to-end on backend and mobile. Backend pytest test_iter49_mkt3.py: 19/19 PASS. Regression iter47 (25/25) + iter48 (26/26) = 51/51 PASS. Backend coverage: (1) Rate card backfilled to 10 items — featured_listing key present (CPA, base=20c, min=5c, max=500c). (2) POST /api/merchant/marketplace/campaigns type=featured: rejects bid_cents=0 with 400 bid_required; creates OK with tagline/bid_cents; owner_user_id stamped, status=active, impressions=0, clicks=0. (3) GET /api/discovery/featured returns items sorted desc by bid_cents (75c ahead of 25c), featured=true flag surfaced, excludes budget-exhausted (paused campaign not returned). (4) POST /api/discovery/featured/{id}/click charges bid to spent_usd + clicks++; 404 for unknown id; auto-pauses on budget exhaustion (bid=50c, budget=$0.30 → spent=0.50 → status=paused); paused row disappears from discovery next call. (5) Impressions counter increments on every discovery list call (2 calls → impressions>=2). (6) Winner Notification: created fresh giveaway → entered → drew → winner user_id in winners list → GET /api/me/notifications returns a giveaway_winner notif with payload{campaign_id,title,sponsor_name,prize_desc} unread. (7) POST /api/me/notifications/{id}/read sets read_at; second read is idempotent (ok=true); unread_only filter excludes it after read. (8) GET /api/me/notifications/unread_count returns integer count. (9) Second draw returns 400 already_drawn (dedupe path is enforced by draw ownership check, not notification dedupe_key — but the enqueue is dedupe-keyed by giveaway_win:<cid>:<uid> so even manual re-triggers would be no-ops). Mobile (Expo web preview, viewport 390×844, demo bearer): /notifications renders notif-inbox with 3 giveaway_winner alerts as notif-item-* rows ('You won: TEST_iter48_gv_… 🎉', 'You won: TEST_iter49_gv_… 🎉', 'You won: Notif Test Giveaway 🎉'); 2 have notif-unread-* orange dots; tapping the first item marks it read (unread count 2→1) and body carries prize_desc + sponsor_name text. Home renders 'FEATURED NEAR YOU' rail with 3 home-featured-{campaign_id} cards. /merchant/marketplace: Launch a campaign → goal picker (mkt-goal-more_customers) → type picker exposes mkt-type-featured alongside coupon_bid/spin/trivia → featured form renders mkt-tagline + mkt-bid + mkt-budget + mkt-launch with 'Higher bids rank first in local discovery' hint. All MKT.3 spec testIDs verified integrated with backend. No new regressions.

critical_code_review_comments: merchant_marketplace.discovery_featured: impressions are incremented on EVERY GET, even for authenticated re-fetches by the same user within a poll cycle. If Home polls this endpoint (or a user pulls to refresh), impressions inflate and the merchant is charged nothing for it (impressions don't spend), but the impressions metric becomes noisy. Consider per-user-per-N-minutes dedupe or moving impression accounting to a separate write.

merchant_marketplace.discovery_featured_click: does NOT enforce idempotency per user. A user can tap the featured card many times and each click charges bid_cents. Consider a brand_featured_clicks collection with unique(user_id, campaign_id, day) to cap spend abuse from a single actor. Currently a hostile client could drain a competitor's budget quickly.

merchant_marketplace.discovery_featured_click: allows anonymous callers (current_user_optional). Combined with lack of idempotency, this means an unauthenticated bot could burn budgets. Recommend either requiring auth or attaching a session/IP-based rate limit.

merchant_marketplace.draw_giveaway: exception around _enqueue is silently swallowed with `except Exception: pass`. If notifications collection has a stale/corrupt index, winners will be drawn but notifications will be silently missed. Consider logging (log.warning) at minimum so a broken pipeline is visible.

routes/notifications._enqueue: dedupe_key uses giveaway_win:<cid>:<uid>. If a merchant deletes and re-creates a campaign with the same id (impossible today — uuid-generated — but worth calling out), notif would silently no-op. Not a bug, just a defensive comment.

mobile/app/notifications.tsx.loadFeed: swallows all errors silently (`catch { /* unauth */ }`). If the request 500s, the empty state renders instead of a retryable error surface. Consider surfacing a subtle 'Couldn't load alerts — tap to retry' row.

mobile/app/(tabs)/home.tsx featured rail: click handler fires POST /discovery/featured/{id}/click via .catch(() => {}) fire-and-forget. If the request fails, the user's tap navigation still occurs (good UX) but a merchant may under-count clicks with no retry. Consider adding a lightweight retry queue for offline scenarios.
